title: SecOps-NG Access Drift Record (SKELETON)
description: Typed shape for one drift record produced when the access drift detector diffs two successive access evidence artifacts in the same `workflow_id` series. SKELETON in this card: the field inventory is pinned, but no detector implementation is shipped and no per-target compiler hook is wired — those land in the F-CP-07 EXTEND-drift CORE-FANOUT sibling. The six delta kinds (`caller_added`, `caller_removed`, `capability_added`, `capability_removed`, `capability_escalated`, `sovereignty_band_changed`) are the surface NIS2 Article 21(2)(i) human-resources / access-control periodic review cares about. Public-bar artefact: principal identifiers stay role-shaped (mirroring the access SCHEMA `caller_identity` discipline), capability tokens stay `verb.resource`-shaped, free-text notes stay role-shaped or URN-shaped, and individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject drift records produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

id.description: Stable per-record identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<previous_artifact_ref>|<current_artifact_ref>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Two detector runs against the same artifact pair collide deliberately.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the drift record. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow identifier — one of the workflow ids declared under `content/playbooks/<workflow-id>/`. The drift record always pins to a single workflow series; cross-workflow drift is intentionally out of scope.

previous_artifact_ref.description: `artifact_id` of the prior access evidence artifact in this `workflow_id` series. SHA-256 hex digest (64 chars).

current_artifact_ref.description: `artifact_id` of the current access evidence artifact being compared against `previous_artifact_ref`. SHA-256 hex digest (64 chars). MUST differ from `previous_artifact_ref` — a drift record against an identical pair is not a drift record.

deltas.description: One entry per detected change between the two artifacts. An empty array is permitted: a deterministic detector that runs against a stable pair and finds no drift still produces a record so downstream consumers see the periodic review walk happened.

detected_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the detector resolved this artifact pair. Format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (no sub-second precision, no offset — UTC only). Carries through to drift-aggregate rollups in the EXTEND-metrics sibling.

kind.description: Which drift surface this delta belongs to. The six-element vocabulary mirrors the surfaces NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) periodic access review cares about and is promoted into `schemas/access_drift_kind.json` alongside the detector wiring. Extending the set is a discussion, not a drive-by change.

principal_id.description: Role-shaped caller identifier the delta is about (mirror of `caller_identity.principal_id` on the access schema). Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline; the pattern pins UPPER_SNAKE_CASE / lower-snake-case / hyphenated identifiers and refuses anything that looks like a credential, an email-with-personal-localpart, or free text.

capability.description: Optional `verb.resource` capability token the delta is about. Present on capability-shaped kinds (`capability_added`, `capability_removed`, `capability_escalated`); absent on caller-shaped (`caller_added`, `caller_removed`) and sovereignty-shaped (`sovereignty_band_changed`) kinds. Mirror of `capabilities[]` item shape on the access schema.

previous.description: Minimal snapshot of the fields relevant to `kind` on the previous side of the change. `null` for `caller_added` and `capability_added`. Carries `{ principal_type, identity_provider? }` for `caller_removed`; `{ tier }` for `capability_escalated`; `{ sovereignty_band }` for `sovereignty_band_changed`. The operator-side `tier` vocabulary and the principal-to-band resolution table both live with the detector wiring; this schema only constrains shape, not vocabulary.

current.description: Minimal snapshot of the fields relevant to `kind` on the current side of the change. `null` for `caller_removed` and `capability_removed`. Carries `{ principal_type, identity_provider? }` for `caller_added`; `{ tier }` for `capability_escalated`; `{ sovereignty_band }` for `sovereignty_band_changed`. The operator-side `tier` vocabulary and the principal-to-band resolution table both live with the detector wiring; this schema only constrains shape, not vocabulary.

note.description: Short free-text rationale field pinning the delta to its inputs. Read by reviewers; not parsed downstream. No individual contact names; role-shaped principal identifiers only, mirroring the access SCHEMA `caller_identity` discipline.

principal_type.description: Mechanical classification of the caller on this side; mirror of `caller_identity.principal_type` on the access schema. Carried on `caller_added` / `caller_removed` deltas.

identity_provider.description: Optional identifier of the identity provider that issued or resolves the caller principal on this side; mirror of `caller_identity.identity_provider` on the access schema. Operator-defined short token.

tier.description: Operator-defined capability privilege tier on this side. Carried on `capability_escalated` deltas. The operator's tier vocabulary lives with the detector wiring; this schema only constrains shape (short lower-snake-case token), not vocabulary.

sovereignty_band.description: Rolled-up sovereignty verdict on the caller's identity-provider hosting endpoint on this side; one of the values promoted in `schemas/sovereignty_band.json`. Carried on `sovereignty_band_changed` deltas.
